items.title: Register the ten ProofStory command-generated artifact filenames in LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES
items.context: packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-registry.ts — add all ten filenames written by the ProofStory intent-hardening block in store.ts (lines ~668-798): original-intent-snapshot.json, milestone-ledger.json, milestone-closeout.json, slice-plan.json, parent-ledger-rollup.json, proofstory.json, intent-collision.json, scope-shrinkage-decision.json, red-evidence.json, spike.json — to the closed filename set consumed by classifyLifecycleArtifact.

happy.desc: After adding the 10 filenames to LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES, build succeeds and classifyLifecycleArtifact returns non-null kind=lifecycle for each of the 10 paths .lattice/story/actives/B-test/{original-intent-snapshot,milestone-ledger,milestone-closeout,slice-plan,parent-ledger-rollup,proofstory,intent-collision,scope-shrinkage-decision,red-evidence,spike}.json; WHY: confirms the registry addition resolves the trigger bug for all 10 names

The existing registered filenames (checklist.json, decision.json, understanding.json, etc.) still classify as lifecycle artifacts after the addition; WHY: confirms the data-only change does not regress existing registrations

edge.desc: Verify the 10 added filenames are an exact character-for-character match with the filenames written by store.ts writeJson calls (lines 672-797) — no typos, no casing differences, no stale renames; WHY: a single-char mismatch silently leaves a name unregistered in the closed Set

No duplicate entries exist in LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES after the addition (the Set deduplicates, but the source list should not contain redundant literals); WHY: duplicates signal a copy-paste error and risk masking a missing distinct name

The deliberately-excluded filenames (grill.json, clusters.json, scope-extension-decisions.json) are NOT added and still classify as null/out_of_scope under an enforce contract; WHY: background.md explicitly carves these out as a separate follow-up — adding them here would silently close a different bug

adversarial.desc: A nested path like .lattice/story/actives/B-test/subdir/original-intent-snapshot.json still returns null (non-top-level artifact), proving the closed-set trust policy (B-b9d0) is preserved for sub-directory paths; WHY: widening the set must not accidentally allow files at arbitrary depth

A path with traversal segments (e.g. .lattice/story/actives/B-test/../B-other/proofstory.json) still returns null, confirming the traversal guard is not bypassed by the new entries; WHY: the registry addition must not weaken the existing ../ rejection

An unknown filename (e.g. evil-intent.json) at the same story-dir top level still returns null after the addition, proving the set is still closed; WHY: the fix must add exactly 10 names and no wildcard or pattern-based relaxation

verificationEvidence.note: Probe A run post-build in the story worktree: classifyLifecycleArtifact returns kind=lifecycle for each of the ten .lattice/story/actives/B-test/<name>.json paths.
Probe B: previously-registered names (checklist.json, decision.json, understanding.json, summary.json, scope-contract.json) still classify kind=lifecycle after the addition — no regression.
Probe C: every one of the ten names appears character-for-character both as a store.ts writeJson(storyId, ...) filename and as a literal registry entry in lifecycle-registry.ts.

items.title: Smoke: fixture story ProofStory artifacts classify as lifecycle_artifact pass instead of out_of_scope
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/scope-contract-smoke.ts — under an enforce contract that does not list story-metadata paths, assert all ten ProofStory artifact paths .lattice/story/actives/<id>/{original-intent-snapshot,milestone-ledger,milestone-closeout,slice-plan,parent-ledger-rollup,proofstory,intent-collision,scope-shrinkage-decision,red-evidence,spike}.json produce scope.lifecycle_artifact pass rows (fails before the registry fix).

happy.desc: After build, running node packages/main/dist/tasks/scope-contract-smoke.js passes with all 10 new assertions: each of the 10 ProofStory artifact paths .lattice/story/actives/B-scope/{original-intent-snapshot,milestone-ledger,milestone-closeout,slice-plan,parent-ledger-rollup,proofstory,intent-collision,scope-shrinkage-decision,red-evidence,spike}.json produces a scope.lifecycle_artifact:<storyId>:<name> row with status=pass and blocking=false; WHY: confirms the smoke pins all 10 names as lifecycle_artifact pass

The existing lifecycleRuntimePositive assertions (summary.json, live-smoke-transcript.json, activity.jsonl) still pass alongside the new 10 assertions; WHY: the new test block must not regress the pre-existing lifecycle/runtime smoke coverage

edge.desc: The test uses an enforce contract (waveContract) whose allowedModify/allowedCreate/allowedTest sets do NOT list story-metadata paths, proving the lifecycle classifier (not an allow-list) is what causes the pass; WHY: if the test accidentally added the paths to allowedModify, the assertion would pass for the wrong reason and would not detect a classifier regression

The existing fail-closed negative assertions (unknown-metadata.json, unowned-source.ts, direct-edit.json at .lattice/story/actives/B-scope/) are preserved and still produce out_of_scope fail rows; WHY: widening the positive set must not silently remove the negative-coverage block that guards the closed-set trust policy

Each new assertion row id follows the pattern scope.lifecycle_artifact:B-scope:<filename> — using the fixture storyId B-scope, not a real story id; WHY: a test using a real storyId could flake when that story is discarded or renamed

adversarial.desc: Before the CHK-001 registry fix (i.e. on current main dist), the 10 new assertions would FAIL with out_of_scope rows — this is the red side of the red-green pair; implementer must record this red state via red_evidence_create before applying the fix; WHY: without the red evidence, the smoke test could be vacuously passing due to a test bug rather than the registry fix

Adding an 11th path to the assertion block with a name NOT in the registry (e.g. .lattice/story/actives/B-scope/not-registered.json) would fail the smoke, proving the test is not accidentally using a wildcard or catch-all; WHY: if the assertion loop were miscoded to pass any story-dir file, it would not detect a missing registry entry

The overall scope check status for the positive block remains pass (not warn or fail) after adding the 10 paths, confirming none of the new entries triggers a violation or unexpected side-effect in checkScopeContract; WHY: a subtle interaction between lifecycle_artifact classification and the enforce mode could produce a warn row that masks a real failure
